content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Use it is with sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, hot, and cold. Model: “It is cloudy this morning, but it is warm now.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use today's weather clearly and politely. One useful response is: “It is cloudy this morning, but it is warm now.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where today's weather is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?
content_sections.title: Use it

exercises.prompt: Read the short message and answer the question about today's weather.

questions.question: How is the weather this morning?

exercises.stimulus: It is cloudy this morning, but it is warm now.

exercises.prompt: Put these two parts in a natural order to make a message about today's weather.
Make a short, personal response about today's weather. Use the lesson language and add one detail that is yours.

criteria: The response communicates a clear meaning about today's weather.
The response uses the allocated language in an understandable form.
The response adds an appropriate personal or invented detail.

language_focus: Use it is with sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, hot, and cold.
objectives: Use it is with sunny, rainy, cloudy, windy, hot, and cold.
Use basic weather descriptions in one short, clear everyday exchange.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about today's weather.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about today's weather. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: What does the speaker have?
listening.transcript: It is rainy and cold today, so I have my umbrella.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Link it is; stress RAIN-y and COLD. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Link it is; stress RAIN-y and COLD.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about today's weather.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using today's weather; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise today's weather?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: It is cloudy this morning, but it is warm now.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about today's weather with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about today's weather. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: It is cloudy this morning, but it is warm now. Submit your draft first.
